items.stem: Explain the term “algin”.
items.answer: A hydrocolloid obtained commercially from brown algae.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a hydrocolloid obtained commercially from brown algae.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as red alga (Rhodophyceae) or brown alga (Phaeophyceae): Gracilaria, Gelidium, Polysiphonia, Ectocarpus.
items.answer: Gracilaria – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Gelidium – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Polysiphonia – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Ectocarpus – brown alga (Phaeophyceae).
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Gracilaria – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Gelidium – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Polysiphonia – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Ectocarpus – brown alga (Phaeophyceae).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a green alga (Chlorophyceae)?
items.answer: Laminaria
items.markingKey: (d) Laminaria is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae), not a green alga (Chlorophyceae).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Volvox is a filamentous alga.”
items.answer: Volvox is a colonial alga; Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Volvox is a colonial alga; Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous.

items.stem: Give two differences between Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.
items.answer: Phaeophyceae: pigments chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and fucoxanthin; cellulose wall covered with algin. Rhodophyceae: stored food is floridean starch; cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. Phaeophyceae – pigments chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and fucoxanthin; cellulose wall covered with algin; Rhodophyceae – stored food is floridean starch; cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters.

items.stem:
An alga shows the following characters: two unequal, laterally attached flagella; stored food is laminarin or mannitol; pigments chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and fucoxanthin.
(i) Identify its class. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were Chlorophyceae? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Phaeophyceae (ii) cellulose wall covered with algin (iii) stored food is starch; cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer)
items.markingKey: (i) Phaeophyceae – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: cellulose wall covered with algin – 1 mark. (iii) for Chlorophyceae: major pigments chlorophyll a and b; stored food is starch; cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer) – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae)?
items.answer: Ectocarpus
items.markingKey: (d) Ectocarpus is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae); the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about algae is correct?
items.answer: Red algae can occur at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.
items.markingKey: (a) Red algae can occur at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates. The other statements are false. Red algae have chlorophyll a, d and r-phycoerythrin; brown algae have fucoxanthin. Volvox is a colonial alga; Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous. Agar is obtained from red algae such as Gelidium and Gracilaria.
options: Red algae can occur at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.
Red algae have chlorophyll a, c and fucoxanthin as the main pigments.
Agar is obtained from brown algae.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic organisms.
Reason (R): Volvox is a filamentous alga.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Volvox is a colonial alga; Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: An alga shows the following characters: two unequal, laterally attached flagella; cellulose wall covered with algin; stored food is laminarin or mannitol. Identify its class. Give a reason.
items.answer: Phaeophyceae
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Phaeophyceae; 1 mark: the features two unequal, laterally attached flagella; cellulose wall covered with algin; stored food is laminarin or mannitol are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
At a seaweed farm on the coast of Tamil Nadu, workers harvest a large brown alga that has a holdfast, a stalk (stipe) and leaf-like fronds.
(i) To which class does it belong? (1 mark)
(ii) Name its stored food and the pigment responsible for its colour. (1 mark)
(iii) Name one hydrocolloid obtained from brown algae and one from red algae, with a use. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Phaeophyceae. (ii) Laminarin or mannitol; fucoxanthin. (iii) Algin from brown algae; carrageen from red algae – used commercially as hydrocolloids (thickeners) in food.
items.markingKey: (i) 1 (ii) ½ + ½ (iii) 1 + 1.

items.stem: Define the term “protonema”.
items.answer: The creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous first stage of the moss gametophyte.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous first stage of the moss gametophyte.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as liverwort or pteridophyte: Dryopteris, Riccia, Psilotum, Marchantia.
items.answer: Dryopteris – pteridophyte; Riccia – liverwort; Psilotum – pteridophyte; Marchantia – liverwort.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Dryopteris – pteridophyte; Riccia – liverwort; Psilotum – pteridophyte; Marchantia – liverwort.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In bryophytes the sporophyte is free-living and dominant.
Reason (R): Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: The sporophyte is attached to and derives nourishment from the photosynthetic gametophyte. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A plant shows these features: thalloid plant body that is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substratum; asexual reproduction by gemmae in gemma cups; sporophyte differentiated into foot, seta and capsule. Identify the group. Give a reason.
items.answer: Liverworts
items.markingKey: 1 mark: liverworts; 1 mark: the features thalloid plant body that is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substratum; asexual reproduction by gemmae in gemma cups; sporophyte differentiated into foot, seta and capsule are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Compare pteridophytes and mosses on any three points.
items.answer: Pteridophytes: sporophyte with true root, stem and leaves; gametophyte is a prothallus; sporangia borne on sporophylls. Mosses: first stage is a filamentous protonema; leafy stage with an upright stem and spirally arranged leaves; well-developed sporophyte with foot, seta and capsule.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. pteridophytes – sporophyte with true root, stem and leaves; gametophyte is a prothallus; sporangia borne on sporophylls; mosses – first stage is a filamentous protonema; leafy stage with an upright stem and spirally arranged leaves; well-developed sporophyte with foot, seta and capsule.

items.stem:
On a trek in Darjeeling, Aditi noticed a soft green carpet on damp rocks and, nearby, a plant with large divided leaves bearing brown dots on the underside.
(i) Name the groups to which the two plants most likely belong. (1 mark)
(ii) What are the brown dots on the leaves of the second plant? (1 mark)
(iii) Give two differences in the life cycles of these two groups. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The carpet – moss (bryophyte); the other – fern (pteridophyte). (ii) Clusters of sporangia (sori) on sporophylls. (iii) In mosses the gametophyte is dominant and the sporophyte depends on it; in ferns the sporophyte is dominant and independent, and the gametophyte is a small prothallus; ferns have vascular tissue.

items.stem: Which term describes compact structures formed when sporophylls are aggregated, as in Selaginella and Equisetum?
items.answer: strobili
items.markingKey: (b) Strobili: compact structures formed when sporophylls are aggregated, as in Selaginella and Equisetum.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about bryophytes and pteridophytes is correct?
items.answer: Sphagnum provides peat used as fuel and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material.
items.markingKey: (a) Sphagnum provides peat used as fuel and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material. The other statements are false. The sporophyte is attached to and derives nourishment from the photosynthetic gametophyte. Bryophytes lack vascular tissue; pteridophytes are the first vascular plants. They are heterosporous, producing megaspores and microspores.
options: Sphagnum provides peat used as fuel and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material.
Bryophytes have well-developed xylem and phloem.
In bryophytes the sporophyte is free-living and dominant.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Selaginella and Salvinia are homosporous.”
items.answer: They are heterosporous, producing megaspores and microspores.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are heterosporous, producing megaspores and microspores.

items.stem: Describe the main features of pteridophytes. Name their four classes with an example each. Why are they important in the evolution of seed habit?
items.answer: Sporophyte dominant with root, stem, leaves and vascular tissue; leaves small (microphylls, Selaginella) or large (macrophylls, ferns); sporangia on sporophylls, sometimes in strobili; spores germinate into prothallus; antheridia and archegonia; water needed. Classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum), Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum). Heterospory (Selaginella, Salvinia) – female gametophyte retained, precursor to seed habit.
items.markingKey: 2 marks features; 2 marks classes; 1 mark seed habit.

items.stem: Give two differences between mosses and pteridophytes.
items.answer: Mosses: first stage is a filamentous protonema; elaborate spore dispersal mechanism. Pteridophytes: xylem and phloem present; sporangia borne on sporophylls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. mosses – first stage is a filamentous protonema; elaborate spore dispersal mechanism; pteridophytes – xylem and phloem present; sporangia borne on sporophylls.

items.stem: Give three points of economic importance of bryophytes.
items.answer: Some mosses provide food for herbivores; Sphagnum gives peat used as fuel and as packing material; mosses and lichens colonise rocks (succession); mosses form dense mats that prevent soil erosion.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three.

items.stem: What is meant by “angiosperms”?
items.answer: Flowering plants in which the seeds are enclosed in fruits.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: flowering plants in which the seeds are enclosed in fruits.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about gymnosperms and angiosperms is correct?
items.answer: Angiosperms range in size from the tiny Wolffia to tall trees of Eucalyptus over 100 metres.
items.markingKey: (c) Angiosperms range in size from the tiny Wolffia to tall trees of Eucalyptus over 100 metres. The other statements are false. Cycas has an unbranched stem; Pinus and Cedrus have branched stems. Gymnosperm seeds are naked; angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits. They do not have an independent free-living existence; they remain within the sporangia on the sporophyte.
options: Male and female gametophytes of gymnosperms are free-living.
Gymnosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits.
Angiosperms range in size from the tiny Wolffia to tall trees of Eucalyptus over 100 metres.
Cycas has a highly branched stem.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a gymnosperm?
items.answer: lily
items.markingKey: (b) Lily is a monocotyledonous plant, not a gymnosperm.

items.stem: A seed plant shows these features: pollen carried by air currents to the ovule opening; no fruit is formed. Identify the group of seed plants. Give a reason.
items.answer: A gymnosperm
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a gymnosperm; 1 mark: the features pollen carried by air currents to the ovule opening; no fruit is formed are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about gymnosperms and angiosperms is incorrect?

items.stem:
A seed plant shows these features: seeds enclosed in fruits; shows double fertilisation; endosperm triploid.
(i) Identify the group of seed plants. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were a gymnosperm? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) An angiosperm (ii) ovules enclosed in an ovary (iii) no fruit is formed; pollen carried by air currents to the ovule opening
items.markingKey: (i) an angiosperm – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: ovules enclosed in an ovary – 1 mark. (iii) for a gymnosperm: ovules exposed on megasporophylls; endosperm haploid; no fruit is formed – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following is a gymnosperm?
items.answer: Pinus
items.markingKey: (d) Pinus is a gymnosperm; the others are not.

items.stem: Describe the main features of gymnosperms. How do they differ from angiosperms?
items.answer: Ovules naked; medium or tall trees and shrubs (Sequoia); tap roots, coralloid roots in Cycas, mycorrhiza in Pinus; needle-like leaves with thick cuticle and sunken stomata; heterosporous; male and female cones/strobili; gametophytes not free-living; pollen grains carried by air; endosperm haploid. Angiosperms: ovules in ovary, flowers, fruits, double fertilisation, triploid endosperm.
items.markingKey: 3 marks features; 2 marks differences.

items.stem: Which term describes sporophylls that bear microsporangia, aggregated into male strobili or cones in gymnosperms?
items.answer: microsporophylls
items.markingKey: (b) Microsporophylls: sporophylls that bear microsporangia, aggregated into male strobili or cones in gymnosperms.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In gymnosperms the ovules are exposed both before and after fertilisation.
Reason (R): Gymnosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Gymnosperm seeds are naked; angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: What is meant by “haplo-diplontic life cycle”?
items.answer: A life cycle in which both the haploid and diploid phases are multicellular and free-living at some stage.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a life cycle in which both the haploid and diploid phases are multicellular and free-living at some stage.

items.answer: some species of Chlamydomonas – plant with a haplontic life cycle; kelps – plant with a haplo-diplontic life cycle; bryophytes – plant with a haplo-diplontic life cycle; Volvox – plant with a haplontic life cycle.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: some species of Chlamydomonas – plant with a haplontic life cycle; kelps – plant with a haplo-diplontic life cycle; bryophytes – plant with a haplo-diplontic life cycle; Volvox – plant with a haplontic life cycle.

items.answer: all seed-bearing plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms)

items.stem: What is the ploidy of a gamete?
items.answer: haploid (n)

items.stem: Distinguish between a haplontic life cycle and a diplontic life cycle on any three points.
items.answer: A haplontic life cycle: free-living haploid gametophyte is dominant; sporophyte is only the one-celled zygote; meiosis in the zygote. A diplontic life cycle: diploid sporophyte is dominant and photosynthetic; gametophyte is few-celled; meiosis forms spores in the sporophyte.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. a haplontic life cycle – free-living haploid gametophyte is dominant; sporophyte is only the one-celled zygote; meiosis in the zygote; a diplontic life cycle – diploid sporophyte is dominant and photosynthetic; gametophyte is few-celled; meiosis forms spores in the sporophyte.

items.stem: What is the ploidy of the prothallus of a fern?
items.answer: haploid (n)
items.markingKey: (d) The prothallus of a fern is haploid (n).

items.stem: Which term describes the diploid plant body that produces haploid spores by meiosis?
items.answer: sporophyte
items.markingKey: (a) Sporophyte: the diploid plant body that produces haploid spores by meiosis.

items.stem: A flowering plant shows these characters: parallel venation in leaves; fibrous root system; flowers usually trimerous. Identify the class. Give a reason.
items.answer: A monocot
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a monocot; 1 mark: the features parallel venation in leaves; fibrous root system; flowers usually trimerous are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Spores are produced by mitosis in the sporophyte.
Reason (R): In pteridophytes the diploid sporophyte is dominant, independent and photosynthetic.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Spores are produced by meiosis in the sporophyte. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Rhodophyceae and Chlorophyceae on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An alga shows the following characters: stored food is starch. Identify its class – Rhodophyceae or Chlorophyceae? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Rhodophyceae: pigments chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin; stored food is floridean starch; cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. Chlorophyceae: major pigments chlorophyll a and b; stored food is starch; cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer). (b) Chlorophyceae.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Chlorophyceae; 1 mark: “stored food is starch” is a feature of Chlorophyceae.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Most brown algae are found in fresh water.”
items.answer: Brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a moss?
items.answer: Selaginella
items.markingKey: (b) Selaginella is a pteridophyte, not a moss.

items.stem: A seed plant shows these features: ovules exposed on megasporophylls; endosperm haploid; no fruit is formed. Identify the group of seed plants. Give a reason.
items.answer: A gymnosperm
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a gymnosperm; 1 mark: the features ovules exposed on megasporophylls; endosperm haploid; no fruit is formed are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A flowering plant shows these characters: reticulate venation in leaves; flowers usually tetramerous or pentamerous; tap root system.
(i) Identify the class. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were a monocot? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) A dicot (ii) two cotyledons in the seed (iii) parallel venation in leaves; flowers usually trimerous
items.markingKey: (i) a dicot – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: two cotyledons in the seed – 1 mark. (iii) for a monocot: one cotyledon in the seed; parallel venation in leaves; fibrous root system – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Define the term “rhizoids”.
items.answer: Unicellular or multicellular root-like structures that attach bryophytes to the substratum.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: unicellular or multicellular root-like structures that attach bryophytes to the substratum.

items.stem: Which of the following is a plant with a haplontic life cycle?
items.answer: Spirogyra
items.markingKey: (b) Spirogyra is a plant with a haplontic life cycle; the others are not.

items.stem: Give three differences between Rhodophyceae and Phaeophyceae.
items.answer: Rhodophyceae: flagella absent; cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters; pigments chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin. Phaeophyceae: pigments chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and fucoxanthin; two unequal, laterally attached flagella; stored food is laminarin or mannitol.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. Rhodophyceae – flagella absent; cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters; pigments chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin; Phaeophyceae – pigments chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and fucoxanthin; two unequal, laterally attached flagella; stored food is laminarin or mannitol.

items.stem: A plant life cycle has these features: free-living haploid gametophyte is dominant; sporophyte is only the one-celled zygote. Identify the pattern. Give a reason.
items.answer: A haplontic life cycle
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a haplontic life cycle; 1 mark: the features free-living haploid gametophyte is dominant; sporophyte is only the one-celled zygote are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is a pteridophyte?
items.answer: Lycopodium
items.markingKey: (d) Lycopodium is a pteridophyte; the others are not.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between an angiosperm and a gymnosperm on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A seed plant shows these features: shows double fertilisation. Identify the group of seed plants – an angiosperm or a gymnosperm? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) An angiosperm: ovules enclosed in an ovary; endosperm triploid; seeds enclosed in fruits. A gymnosperm: ovules exposed on megasporophylls; endosperm haploid; no fruit is formed. (b) An angiosperm.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: an angiosperm; 1 mark: “shows double fertilisation” is a feature of an angiosperm.

items.stem: What is meant by “isogamous reproduction”?
items.answer: Fusion of two gametes similar in size.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: fusion of two gametes similar in size.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct sequence in the life cycle of a fern?
items.answer: meiosis in sporangium → spores (n) → prothallus (n)
items.markingKey: (c) meiosis in sporangium → spores (n) → prothallus (n). The sporophyte forms spores by meiosis; the spore gives the gametophyte; gametes fuse to form the zygote.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as dicotyledonous plant or gymnosperm: mango, pea, Ginkgo, mustard.
items.answer: mango – dicotyledonous plant; pea – dicotyledonous plant; Ginkgo – gymnosperm; mustard – dicotyledonous plant.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: mango – dicotyledonous plant; pea – dicotyledonous plant; Ginkgo – gymnosperm; mustard – dicotyledonous plant.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about bryophytes and pteridophytes is incorrect?
items.answer: Bryophytes have well-developed xylem and phloem.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “Bryophytes have well-developed xylem and phloem.” Correct form: Bryophytes lack vascular tissue; pteridophytes are the first vascular plants.
options: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues, xylem and phloem.
In pteridophytes the main plant body is a sporophyte differentiated into root, stem and leaves.
Bryophytes have well-developed xylem and phloem.
In bryophytes the main plant body is haploid and the gametophyte is dominant.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as green alga (Chlorophyceae) or red alga (Rhodophyceae): Chara, Ulothrix, Gracilaria, Chlamydomonas.
items.answer: Chara – green alga (Chlorophyceae); Ulothrix – green alga (Chlorophyceae); Gracilaria – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Chlamydomonas – green alga (Chlorophyceae).
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Chara – green alga (Chlorophyceae); Ulothrix – green alga (Chlorophyceae); Gracilaria – red alga (Rhodophyceae); Chlamydomonas – green alga (Chlorophyceae).

items.stem:
A plant shows these features: first stage is a filamentous protonema; well-developed sporophyte with foot, seta and capsule; elaborate spore dispersal mechanism.
(i) Identify the group. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were pteridophytes? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Mosses (ii) leafy stage with an upright stem and spirally arranged leaves (iii) sporangia borne on sporophylls; xylem and phloem present
items.markingKey: (i) mosses – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: leafy stage with an upright stem and spirally arranged leaves – 1 mark. (iii) for pteridophytes: sporophyte with true root, stem and leaves; xylem and phloem present; sporangia borne on sporophylls – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which term describes a life cycle in which both the haploid and diploid phases are multicellular and free-living at some stage?
items.answer: haplo-diplontic life cycle
items.markingKey: (a) Haplo-diplontic life cycle: a life cycle in which both the haploid and diploid phases are multicellular and free-living at some stage.

items.stem: A flowering plant shows these characters: two cotyledons in the seed; flowers usually tetramerous or pentamerous. Identify the class. Give a reason.
items.answer: A dicot
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a dicot; 1 mark: the features two cotyledons in the seed; flowers usually tetramerous or pentamerous are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Spores are produced by mitosis in the sporophyte.
Reason (R): In bryophytes the dominant phase is the haploid gametophyte.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Spores are produced by meiosis in the sporophyte. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Chlorophyceae and Rhodophyceae on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An alga shows the following characters: cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer). Identify its class – Chlorophyceae or Rhodophyceae? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Chlorophyceae: major pigments chlorophyll a and b; stored food is starch; cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer). Rhodophyceae: pigments chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin; stored food is floridean starch; cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. (b) Chlorophyceae.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Chlorophyceae; 1 mark: “cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer)” is a feature of Chlorophyceae.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Red algae have chlorophyll a, c and fucoxanthin as the main pigments.”
items.answer: Red algae have chlorophyll a, d and r-phycoerythrin; brown algae have fucoxanthin.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Red algae have chlorophyll a, d and r-phycoerythrin; brown algae have fucoxanthin.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a moss?
items.answer: Dryopteris
items.markingKey: (d) Dryopteris is a pteridophyte, not a moss.

items.stem: A seed plant shows these features: seeds enclosed in fruits; shows double fertilisation. Identify the group of seed plants. Give a reason.
items.answer: An angiosperm
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an angiosperm; 1 mark: the features seeds enclosed in fruits; shows double fertilisation are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A flowering plant shows these characters: tap root system; two cotyledons in the seed; flowers usually tetramerous or pentamerous.
(i) Identify the class. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were a monocot? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) A dicot (ii) reticulate venation in leaves (iii) flowers usually trimerous; fibrous root system
items.markingKey: (i) a dicot – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: reticulate venation in leaves – 1 mark. (iii) for a monocot: one cotyledon in the seed; parallel venation in leaves; fibrous root system – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: What is meant by “prothallus”?
items.answer: The small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte of pteridophytes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte of pteridophytes.

items.stem: Which of the following is a plant with a haplo-diplontic life cycle?
items.answer: kelps
items.markingKey: (c) Kelps is a plant with a haplo-diplontic life cycle; the others are not.

items.stem: Compare Chlorophyceae and Rhodophyceae on any three points.
items.answer: Chlorophyceae: two to eight equal, apical flagella; major pigments chlorophyll a and b; cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer). Rhodophyceae: cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters; pigments chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin; stored food is floridean starch.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. Chlorophyceae – two to eight equal, apical flagella; major pigments chlorophyll a and b; cell wall of cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer); Rhodophyceae – cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters; pigments chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin; stored food is floridean starch.
